# Article image — the graphic designer's procedure

Every article and news image on «الجون» is chosen, vetted and composed by the
**graphic-designer** agent (user rule 2026-11-08: «عايز graphic-designer agent
يكون مسئول عن الصور الخاصة بالمقالات والاخبار»). The writer (sports-writer)
hands you the story and uses what you return; it never picks an image itself.
Read this file in full at the start of every image job. The rules below were
MOVED here word for word from the three article prompts — each one is a real
mistake that shipped once; none is optional.

## What you get, what you return
- **You get** from the writer: the piece's `kind` (news / preview / report / round), the final headline, every person and club it names (Arabic exactly as the article writes them, plus the English name), the date, a two-sentence summary of who is in the story NOW, and - for a round piece - the round's leader and the grounds of its matches. (A match piece whose brief already carries `brief.image` never reaches you: the writer uses that card as-is.)
- **You return**, as the LAST four lines of your answer, exactly:
  `image_url: https://elgoon.com/media/<file>`
  `image_credit: <the credit, verbatim>`
  `files: <every path the writer must git add, space-separated>`
  `why: <one line: the subject, the licence, the rule that decided>`
- You never write or edit the article, never touch `data/articles.json`, never run `article_put.py`, never commit or push - the writer does all of that with your four lines.
- Only the placeholder has an empty credit. If you truly find nothing, say so in `why` and return the fallback the rules below name - never an unvetted photo to fill the slot.
- Look at every image you return (the Read tool) before you return it.

## 1. Which kind of image - the headline test (news pieces)
**MATCHUP STORIES USE OUR CARD, NOT A PHOTO (user rule 2026-10-08: «الأخبار اللى عن المواجهات تعمل صور بالقالب للفرق المتنافسة وتستخدمها»).** **THE HEADLINE TEST decides.** Read your own headline: if it names a PERSON - a player, a coach, an official, a referee speaking, anyone quoted («عبدالفتاح: …», «الزمالك يحذر بانزا…», «هالاند يدعو…») - or ONE club doing something, the image is that person's or club's own photo under the rules below, NEVER the card, even when the body is all about the coming match. The card is ONLY for a story whose subject is the FIXTURE itself and whose headline names the two teams or the match and nobody else: the date/venue/broadcast announcement, the FA naming the referee crew (an announcement, not a person's comment on it), both squad lists, the result. Two real misses (user, 2026-10-09): «الزمالك يحذر شيكو بانزا من التأخر في العودة قبل قمة الأهلي» and «عبدالفتاح: الأهلي لم يعترض على حكم القمة.. واستقالة عاشور» both shipped with the derby card; the first needed a Zamalek/Banza photo, the second an Al Ahly photo. **A story about a CLUB or one of its officials/board (the headline names the club or an official speaking for it) takes the club's IDENTITY IMAGE from `data/team_photos.json`** (user, 2026-10-15: four Zamalek stories in two days still shipped the old blue club card while one took the identity image - he asked why): the entry whose `subject` starts with «شعار» for that club - `media/<slug>-identity-card.jpg` for every curated club and the NT, `media/al-ahly-red-castle-card.jpg` for Al Ahly - with its `credit` «الصورة: تصميم الجون». **The old blue `club-<slug>-card.jpg` files are RETIRED for every club that has an identity image; do not generate or reuse them.** The identity image is the club's standing image, so the VARIETY rule does not apply to it (it may illustrate consecutive club stories) - variety is for photos of people. A story about a PLAYER takes the player's own vetted photo under the rules below (the editor's folder first); when no free photo of him exists, use the club's identity image instead of a stadium or a crowd. The matchup card: `python matchup_card.py --teams "<home>" "<away>" --out media/matchup-<short-ascii-slug>.jpg` (Arabic names exactly as the site writes them, home side first when known; a NEW filename per article). The script finds the fixture in our data and draws the clubs' colours, competition, round, date and venue - or just the two names when the fixture is not in our data. Open it with the Read tool, then `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/<that file>` and `image_credit` = «الصورة: تصميم الجون». No photo search, no hero-crop check (the card is built for both crops). Transfers, contracts, awards, personal or club-business stories are NOT matchup stories: they keep the photo rules below.

## 2. Match pieces (preview / report) without a brief image
- `image_url` + `image_credit` (no `brief.image`): prefer a photo of the curated club from the editor's folder — an entry of that club in `data/team_photos.json`, NOT one used by the last 3 articles about that club (search data/articles.json) — never a media/ file outside that registry (user rule 2026-10-18); otherwise a Wikimedia Commons photo per the usual rules (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / PD only, the player in the CURRENT club's kit or the club's stadium, ≥1200px wide preferred (Discover threshold), ≥800px minimum, view it with the Read tool, check the 1544x400 hero crop keeps heads intact, Arabic credit). Never a rival club's colours, never a former-club shirt.
- **THE FOLDER PATH IS NOT EXEMPT**, and it is the likelier source: when you take a `data/team_photos.json` entry, run the self-test on ITS `credit`/`subject`/`year` too. Never trust the FILENAME — `mohamed-chibi-pyramids.jpg` was a Morocco photo. And when you save a new file, name it after what it SHOWS, never after the club the article is about. **A media/ file that is not in data/team_photos.json must not be used** (user rule 2026-10-18) — the folders are the only pool, and what the editor deleted from them is gone from the registry.
- **CREDIT SELF-TEST (added 2026-09-08 — this preview type is exactly where it failed).** Before saving, re-read the `image_credit` you are about to write. If it names another club, another country or another era — «خلال مشواره الكروي في المغرب», «بقميص غيور إيتو المجري», «خلال فترة تدريبه ماميلودي صن داونز», «قناة النادي الأهلي» on a Pyramids story, «صورة أرشيفية» — the photo is WRONG; discard it and pick another. A caption admitting the picture is from elsewhere is a confession, not attribution. Real case: «قبل المباراة: بيراميدز يواجه الجونة» shipped with Mohamed Chibi in his Morocco years and the credit said so. When no current-club photo exists, the only allowed images are the club's own STADIUM (a home preview: use the host's ground) or the player in his NATIONAL TEAM kit.

## 3. Round pieces («الجولة بالأرقام»)
- `image_url` + `image_credit`: the same rules as every article (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / PD; no rival colours; the living-story test). FIRST look in `data/team_photos.json` for a photo of the round's LEADER (the editor's own team-photos/<club>/ folders, credit verbatim from the entry); then prefer an already-vetted media/ photo of the round's LEADER or of the stadium of a match in the round, reusing its credit verbatim from data/articles.json, data/media_credits.json or data/team_photos.json; never a file with no recorded credit. Last resort: `https://elgoon.com/media/ph-pitch.svg` with an empty credit.

## 4. Licence, relevance, identity
- Images MUST be freely licensed (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / public domain from Wikimedia Commons). Never press photos, Getty/agency images, or official club logos/crests.
- The image MUST be topically relevant: prefer (in order) a free photo of the exact player/coach mentioned in the story, then the named club's stadium/team photo. If NEITHER exists, use the branded placeholder `https://elgoon.com/media/ph-pitch.svg` with an EMPTY image_credit — never a stadium/crowd/atmosphere photo of some OTHER venue. A caption that needs a disclaimer like "لا تعبر بالضرورة عن..." is the proof the photo is wrong: if you find yourself writing one, switch to the placeholder. (Rule tightened 2026-08-23 after a Cairo-stadium crowd photo shipped on an El Gouna loan story.)
- CLUB COLOURS MUST MATCH THE STORY: never illustrate a story about club X with a crowd or kit in club Y's colours. Red shirts read as الأهلي, so a red-clad crowd is WRONG on a Zamalek story — including Egypt NT crowds (Egypt also plays in red). Zamalek = white, Al Ahly = red. Identify the dominant shirt colour and reject on mismatch no matter how good the licence.
- THE PHOTO MUST SHOW THE NAMED PERSON: a story about player X must use a photo of player X himself — a photo of a DIFFERENT player in the same club kit is WRONG. The Commons file NAME or file DESCRIPTION must explicitly name the player; generic "Ahly player" identification is NOT acceptable. If no free photo of the named player exists, fall back IN THIS ORDER: (1) **the club's folder** — any entry of that club in `data/team_photos.json` (the editor's vetted photos of the club: scenes, stadium, the identity image); for منتخب مصر the `egypt` folder — this is where the Egypt-imagery expectation is met now (rule of 2026-08-23), (2) the club's identity image from the same file, (3) ONLY for a subject with NO folder (a non-curated club, a federation, a venue) and nothing free on Commons: the branded placeholder `https://elgoon.com/media/ph-pitch.svg` with an empty image_credit — it is the LAST resort, not a convenient default, and a curated club's story never ends there (the publish tool fills the folder image itself). **NEVER reuse a file from media/ that is not in data/team_photos.json** (user rule 2026-10-18: «خلي اعتمادك عليه وبلاش تروح لـ media»): media/ is the published store, the folders are the only pool you choose from, and a photo the editor deleted from a folder is out of the registry on the next sync — so do not go around it. There is NO "any Egyptian stadium on a club story" fallback. Write the credit line for what the photo ACTUALLY shows. Never guess identity from kit colours alone (a team photo of the OPPONENT in red is not Egypt), and never pick between same-name people/clubs (لييج/ستاندرد لييج، الأهلي مصر/جدة، حسام حسن الكابتن/المحامي) by guessing. A MATCHING NAME IS NOT ENOUGH: Egyptian football is full of namesakes, and Commons photos naturally exist for the FAMOUS one — the file's description must also match the story person's CURRENT ROLE + CLUB + ERA. A story about «محمد بركات المدير الفني لإنبي» must NOT use the Commons photos of محمد بركات نجم الأهلي السابق (this exact mistake shipped 2026-08-24 and the user caught it live). When the story's person is a coach/official who shares a name with a famous player, assume every Commons hit is the famous player unless the description explicitly says otherwise — and fall back to (1)/(2)/(3) instead.
- BEWARE NAME CLASHES: Egyptian football has many same-name players (e.g. إبراهيم عادل: an Ahly academy youngster AND a famous international abroad are different people). Rules: (a) never write a player's career history from your own recollection of the name — state only biography the fetched sources state about THIS story's player; (b) read the sources' qualifiers (ناشئ / الشاب / فريق الشباب / قطاع الناشئين); (c) if sources disagree on a basic attribute, say so or omit it; (d) when the story is about a namesake, add one sentence distinguishing him; (e) in a name-clash story the obvious Commons hit is probably the WRONG person.

## 5. Finding and vetting a photo
Otherwise: image via Wikimedia Commons API (commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php, list=search srnamespace=6, then prop=imageinfo&iiprop=url|size|extmetadata to verify LicenseShortName is CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / Public domain).
- CURRENT-CLUB KIT (user rule 2026-09-04): the player must be shown in the kit/training gear of the club the story is about (or his national team, or neutral clothing) — NEVER in a FORMER club's shirt (Chiesa in Juventus stripes on a Liverpool story was rejected). Check the photo's date against the player's transfer history; Commons descriptions like "arriving at ... prior to the match between X and Y" date the photo. If the only free photo of him is in an old club's kit, use the OTHER player/coach named in the story, the club's stadium, or an already-vetted media/ photo of the club instead.
- **CREDIT SELF-TEST — do this before you save, it is the check that actually catches a wrong photo (added 2026-09-08).** Re-read the `image_credit` you are about to write, as a reader would. If it names another club, another country or another era — «خلال مشواره الكروي في المغرب», «بقميص غيور إيتو المجري», «خلال فترة تدريبه ماميلودي صن داونز», «قناة النادي الأهلي» on a Pyramids story, «صورة أرشيفية» — then **the photo is wrong, discard it**. A caption that admits the picture is from somewhere else is not attribution, it is a confession. The user caught exactly this on 2026-09-08: a Pyramids preview illustrated with Mohamed Chibi in his Morocco years, and the credit said so out loud. The ONLY images allowed when no current-club photo exists are: the club's own stadium, or the player in his NATIONAL TEAM kit (say so in the credit).
- **THE LIVING-STORY TEST — the person in the photo must still be IN the story (user rule 2026-09-12, caught live).** A preview of a match being played that same day shipped with Steven Gerrard, retired since 2016, and every existing check passed it: the club was right, the shirt was Liverpool's, the file was honestly named, and the credit was accurate — «صورة: ستيفن جيرارد، أسطورة ليفربول السابق ... عام 2014». Accuracy is not relevance. So before saving, ask of the person in the photo: **is he part of THIS event?** For a match piece that means he is in one of the two squads TODAY. For a news piece it means he is the person the story is about, now. If the answer is no, the photo is wrong however true its caption is. **Words that disqualify a photo unless the article is ABOUT that person: «السابق», «أسطورة», «اعتزل», «سابقًا» — and any photo year three seasons old or more on a piece about a current match.** A club legend illustrating today's fixture reads to a reader as a mistake, because it is one: it says we had nothing current to show. The allowed fallbacks are unchanged and in this order — a current squad member, the HOST club's stadium, the player in his national-team kit. The one case where a «السابق» photo is right is when that person IS the subject: the same Gerrard photo is correct on «جيرارد يعود إلى مرشحي تدريب طرابزون سبور».
- **THE EDITOR'S TEAM FOLDERS COME FIRST (user ask 2026-10-13: «فولدرات بأسماء الفرق هنحط فيه صور للفرق انت تستخدمهم في الأخبار»).** `data/team_photos.json` lists photos the editor put BY HAND into `team-photos/<club>/` and `team_photos.py` copied into media/ with the credit HE wrote. He vetted them, so for a story about a curated club they are the FIRST choice - before the club card and before any Wikimedia search: read the file, take the entries whose `club` is the club in the headline. A story about a PLAYER prefers an entry whose `subject` names him, else any entry of his club; a story about the club or one of its officials takes any entry of the club (the club card is the fallback when the folder has nothing). `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/<file>`, `image_credit` = the entry's `credit` VERBATIM. The variety rule still applies (not the file the last 3 articles about that club used - search data/articles.json) and so does the living-story test on the entry's `subject`/`year`. Each entry carries its `width`: prefer one of 1200 or more (Google Discover's floor, 2026-11-04) and take a narrower one only when no wide entry fits the subject. These folders do NOT override the matchup card for FIXTURE stories (the headline test still decides), and an empty list for the club means: fall through to the rules below exactly as before.
- **THE PHOTO LIBRARY (added 2026-09-12).** `data/media_credits.json` is a second, equally valid place a credit can live: free photos stocked BY HAND in the Oracle app (pages 30 and 31 of app 200) and pushed here with their licence, subject, club and year. Treat an entry there exactly like a credit found in data/articles.json - it is vetted, and its `year` and `subject` are what the living-story test needs. **This does not change how you pick a photo**: keep fetching fresh from Wikimedia for the story in front of you. The library is a shelf to fall back on, most useful for clubs where a fresh search keeps coming up empty.
- `python audit_images.py` (run from the site root) applies both checks — wrong club and living-story — to every published article and prints the suspects. Run it if you are unsure about a reused photo. Fixing a photo on an ALREADY published article is not done by hand: add an entry to `data/image_fixes.json` and the D1 Admin workflow's `fix-images` task applies it.
- **FILENAME HONESTY (same incident).** Name the file after what the picture SHOWS, never after the club the article is about. That Chibi photo was saved as `mohamed-chibi-pyramids.jpg`, so the next Pyramids article searching media/ found it by name and reused it — one bad photo became two bad articles. A Morocco-era photo is `mohamed-chibi-morocco.jpg`. Never put a club's name in a filename unless the photo shows that club.
- **NO REUSE FROM media/ (user rule 2026-10-18).** The only vetted pool is `data/team_photos.json` (the editor's `team-photos/<club>/` folders); use an entry's `file` and `credit` VERBATIM and run the credit self-test on that text too. A media/ file that is not in that registry is not yours to use, whatever data/articles.json says about it — the editor removes from the folders what he does not want, and that must stick.
- IMAGE VARIETY (user rule 2026-08-30): before settling on a photo, check what the PREVIOUS articles about this same player/coach/club used — search data/articles.json for the subject's name and note those articles' image_url filenames. Pick a photo DIFFERENT from the one used last time for this subject: another suitable Commons photo of him, or a different already-vetted media/ photo of the same subject. Variety NEVER overrides the relevance/licence/quality rules above — if only one suitable free photo of the subject exists, reusing it is better than a placeholder or a wrong photo.
- Quality is mandatory: at least 1200px wide (Google Discover only picks articles with images ≥1200px; 800-1199 is acceptable ONLY when no wider free photo of the right subject exists); never tiny crops from group photos. For huge originals request a thumbnail via &iiurlwidth=1280 (only standard thumb widths like 1280/1920 are accepted).
- ALWAYS OPEN THE DOWNLOADED IMAGE WITH THE Read TOOL AND LOOK AT IT BEFORE PUBLISHING. Check: correct subject, sharp, right club colours, face visible, nothing embarrassing.
- HERO CROP CHECK: the article page renders the image with object-fit:cover; object-position:50% 18%; max-height 400px at up to ~1544px wide. Simulate that crop with PIL at 1544x400 AND 390x400 and LOOK at both — the player's head must never be sliced. For portrait/square sources, build a ~2.1:1 canvas: paste the photo centered over a blurred+darkened enlarged copy of itself (pillarbox), then re-check.
- If the image looks sideways, rotate the pixels and view again. A gentle contrast/colour/sharpness enhance (~1.1-1.2) is fine for CC/PD as long as attribution stays.
- **WHERE A NEW PHOTO LIVES (user ask 2026-10-18: «فولدرات للفرق وصورهم داخلها، والبوستات والمقالات ياخدوا من الصور دى»).** A photo you download for a story about a CURATED CLUB or the NT goes into THAT CLUB'S FOLDER, never straight into media/: save it as `team-photos/<slug>/<short-descriptive-ascii>.jpg` (slug = the club's /team/<slug> page: al-ahly, zamalek, pyramids, real-madrid, barcelona, man-united, man-city, arsenal, liverpool, chelsea, trabzonspor; `egypt` for the NT), append its line to that folder's `credits.txt` — `<file> | <the Arabic credit> | <photo year> | <who or what is in it>` — then run `python team_photos.py`: it shrinks the photo in place, copies it to `media/<slug>-<stem>.jpg` and records it in `data/team_photos.json`. Read the new entry back and use ITS `file` as image_url (`https://elgoon.com/media/<file>`) and its `credit` verbatim. This is how the editor sees every photo his clubs' stories used: one folder per club. A photo for anything else (another club, a federation, a venue) still goes straight into media/ with a short descriptive ascii filename, prefer <1 MB, image_url = "https://elgoon.com/media/<filename>" and image_credit = Arabic attribution: "صورة: <الموضوع> — <المصور/المصدر>، رخصة <License> (ويكيميديا كومنز)".

## 5b. The club shirt and the mood
- **THE STORY'S CLUB SHIRT (user rule 2026-11-08: «تخلى اللاعب لو بتتكلم على فريقه يكون لابس فانلة فريقه»).** When the story is about a player AT his club (a match, a transfer, a contract, his club form), search WITH the club: `python find_photo.py "<English name>" --club "<the club in English>" --since <the year he joined> --out /tmp/cands`. It walks Commons' «<player> in <year>» albums and «<player> with <club>» categories and lists the photos filed under the club first, tagged CLUB (green on the contact sheet). The tag is a hint: LOOK at each one and keep only a photo where the shirt you SEE is that club's (match kit, training kit or club jacket), the person is identifiable (a wide shot from the stands is not), and the date is after he joined. Only when no such free photo exists may his national-team shirt stand in - the credit says so («بقميص منتخب مصر») and `why:` says the club search found none. A former club's shirt: never. When the story is about his NATIONAL TEAM, the national-team shirt is the right shirt. **Never edit a photo to change a shirt, a crest, a sponsor, a face or an expression** - choosing the photo is the only tool; an edited news photo is a fake one.
- **THE STORY'S MOOD (user rule 2026-11-08: «لو الخبر حزين تخلى الصورة حزينة ولو الخبر حلو تخلى الصورة مفرحة»).** Read the mood from the headline: **happy** = a win, a goal, a title, a renewal, a signing, an award, a return from injury; **sad** = a loss, an elimination, an injury, criticism, a sacking, a ban, a death; **neutral** = everything else (an announcement, a fixture, a squad list, a farewell such as a retirement - unless the story is a mourning). Then: (1) **choose the expression** - among the photos that pass every rule above, a smile or a celebration for happy, a serious, tired or dejected face for sad; never a laughing face on bad news, never a slumped one on good news; when the only valid photo of the person has the wrong expression, take a neutral face rather than the wrong one; (2) pass `--mood happy|sad|neutral` to `news_image.py` (section 7) - it grades colour and light only: warmer and brighter for happy; drained, darker and cooler with a slate panel and a steel edge for sad. The grade does not fix a wrong expression (a smiling face stays smiling in grey), so step (1) comes first. Say the mood in `why:`.

## 6. Filenames
- UNIQUE media/ FILENAME per article: pick a filename that does not already exist in media/. If `git status` shows your new image as M (modified) instead of ?? (new), you just overwrote another article's photo — pick another name.

## 7. Compose the news image (style C)
- **COMPOSE THE NEWS IMAGE (user choice 2026-11-08: «Style C»; it replaces `hero_card.py`).** A photo of a PERSON never ships raw. Once it has passed every rule above (identity, licence, living-story, credit self-test), run `python news_image.py --photo <the photo file> --kicker "<1-3 Arabic words: the club the STORY is about, the competition, or the story type>" --mood <happy|sad|neutral> --out media/news-<short-ascii>.jpg --debug` (the mood from section 5b). It never cuts the person out and never uses a club's crest or colours: our navy panel carries the label and the wordmark, and the photo fills the rest, framed around the face (it strips a blurred pillarbox first, finds the person, then his face). OPEN BOTH FILES with the Read tool. `<out>-face.jpg` must show the green box on the NAMED person's face - not a team-mate, not the crowd; if it is anywhere else, re-run with `--focus x,y` (his face's position as fractions of the photo's width and height). Then the image itself: the right person, head whole, the label spelled right. `image_url` = `https://elgoon.com/media/news-<...>.jpg`, `image_credit` = the photo's credit line VERBATIM + « — تركيب: الجون» (the licence attribution stays; only the composition is ours). `files:` = the source photo (under its folder/registry rules above) and the news image - delete the `-face.jpg` check file, it is never committed. A NEW name per article. The matchup card, the identity images and stadium or scene photos are NOT composed. **`hero_card.py` is never run** (2026-11-08, article 1104: its cutout left a team-mate's head floating behind Marmoush, it drew official club crests, and it set a national-team shirt on a club's colours). A WIDER SEARCH when the name search finds nothing good: `python find_photo.py "<English name>" --category "<Commons category, e.g. the player's name>" --out /tmp/cands` walks Commons (text + category albums) and Openverse (Flickr + Wikimedia, licence-filtered), prints the candidates widest-first and writes `/tmp/cands.png`, a contact sheet to look at, and `/tmp/cands.json` with each file's `url`, licence and author. It finds candidates; every vetting rule above still applies to the one you pick.
